Shared rule with Menahem and Pekahiah (rival reign), 752–740 BC
Rival reign from 752 BC; sole king 740/739 to 732/731
Printed form: c. 737–732 (p. 22); 6 years or less against the Hebrew text's 20.

Mack: “in the confusion which followed the death of Jeroboam, Pekah established his authority” over the land east of the Jordan, and the numbers of 2 Kings 15:27, 32 and 16:1 count from that year.[21]
A rival reign counted from 752 BC
R. C. Young's tables (Thiele as revised)
Young's table shows Pekah's reign overlapping Menahem's and Pekahiah's from 752 BC and his sole reign from 740/739.[1]
Ussher gives Pekah twenty full years, 759–739 BC, and places a nine-year “Anarchy” after his death before Hoshea reigned quietly.[2]
2 Kings 15:25–31 2 Kings 15:37 2 Kings 16:5–9 2 Chronicles 28:5–15 Isaiah 7:1–9 1 Chronicles 5:26
Scripture gives no age, mother or burial for Pekah.

Kings does not mention Assyria in Pekah's fall; Tiglath-pileser's annals say “they deposed” him and that Tiglath-pileser set Hoshea over them (see Outside the Bible). Neither record makes the other wrong.
